label: Age under 20 (teenage pregnancy / young primi)
source: MoHFW PMSMA: "young primi (less than 20 years)"; 2024 HRP list: teenage pregnancy. MoHFW SBA 2010 uses under 18 – doctor to confirm whether for all pregnancies or first only

label: Age over 35
source: MoHFW PMSMA: "elderly gravida (more than 35 years)". ACOG / FOGSI-ICOG use 35 or older – doctor to confirm whether exactly 35 should be flagged

label: Height under 145 cm (short stature)
source: MoHFW/MWCD MCP Card guidebook 2018: under 145 cm is an obstetric risk; 2024 HRP list: short stature

label: BMI 35 or more (severe obesity)
source: FOGSI-ICOG ANC GCPR: BMI ≥ 35 at first contact is high risk

label: BMI 30 or more (obesity)
source: WHO / RCOG GTG 72: obesity BMI ≥ 30. Not a named GoI HRP category; MoHFW GDM guideline uses Asian cut-offs (obese > 25) – doctor to decide on a lower tier

label: BMI under 18.5 (underweight)
source: WHO / MoHFW GDM guideline BMI table: underweight < 18.5. FOGSI-ICOG treats BMI < 18 as high – doctor to confirm level

label: Weight under 45 kg
source: MoHFW SBA/ANM guideline: women under 45 kg need extra nutrition and follow-up

label: Previous caesarean section
source: MoHFW PMSMA HRP list: previous LSCS (deliver at a CEmOC facility)

label: Grand multipara (4 or more previous births)
source: MoHFW SBA 2010: grand multipara = 4 or more; PMSMA HRP list: grand multipara; NICE: parity ≥ 4. Classic definition is ≥ 5 – doctor to confirm

label: Three or more previous miscarriages / abortions
source: MoHFW SBA 2010: ≥ 3 spontaneous abortions – refer (bad obstetric history). The A count may include losses that were not spontaneous – doctor to confirm

label: Two previous miscarriages / abortions
source: ESHRE / ASRM: recurrent pregnancy loss from 2 losses (RCOG: 3). The A count may include losses that were not spontaneous – doctor to confirm

label: Previous stillbirth or newborn death
source: MoHFW SBA/ANC guidelines: previous stillbirth / neonatal loss; PMSMA: bad obstetric history

label: Previous preterm birth
source: PMSMA: bad obstetric history (previous preterm)

label: Pre-eclampsia / eclampsia in a previous pregnancy
source: MoHFW SBA/ANC guidelines; FOGSI-GESTOSIS-ICOG HDP score

label: Previous baby with a congenital anomaly
source: PMSMA HRP list: congenital malformation / bad obstetric history

label: Previous obstructed labour
source: MoHFW SBA/ANC guidelines: previous obstructed labour

label: Previous bleeding after delivery (PPH)
source: MoHFW SBA/ANC guidelines: previous PPH / APH

label: Rh sensitisation in a previous pregnancy
source: MoHFW SBA/ANC guidelines: iso-immunisation (Rh −ve) in the previous pregnancy

label: Previous baby under 2.5 kg
source: MoHFW SBA/ANC guidelines: previous low-birth-weight baby – refer to MO

label: Previous baby over 4 kg
source: MoHFW SBA/ANC guidelines: previous baby > 4–4.5 kg – screen for diabetes; doctor to confirm cut-off

label: Rh-negative blood group
source: MoHFW PMSMA HRP list: Rh negative. NICE/ACOG treat unsensitised Rh-negative as routine care with anti-D – doctor to confirm level

label: Diabetes (known before pregnancy)
source: PMSMA: GDM and any current systemic illness; MoHFW SBA: diabetes

label: Chronic high blood pressure
source: PMSMA: chronic hypertension antedating pregnancy or before 20 weeks

label: Heart disease
source: PMSMA: current systemic illness; MoHFW SBA / MCP card: heart disease (specialist at FRU)

label: Kidney disease
source: MoHFW SBA systemic illness list; FOGSI-GESTOSIS-ICOG HDP score (3 points)

label: Autoimmune disease (e.g. SLE, antiphospholipid syndrome)
source: FOGSI-GESTOSIS-ICOG HDP score (3 points)

label: Thrombophilia (clotting disorder)
source: FOGSI-GESTOSIS-ICOG HDP score (3 points)

label: Thyroid disease
source: PMSMA HRP list: hypothyroidism. ATA: well-treated hypothyroidism adds little risk – doctor may choose moderate

label: Epilepsy
source: MoHFW SBA: convulsions (epilepsy); RCOG GTG 68

label: Mental health condition
source: FOGSI-GESTOSIS-ICOG HDP score (3 points) – doctor to confirm level

label: Tuberculosis
source: MoHFW SBA / MCP card: tuberculosis; GoI TB-maternal health framework

label: HIV
source: MoHFW PMSMA HRP list: syphilis/HIV positive

label: Syphilis
source: MoHFW PMSMA HRP list: syphilis/HIV positive

label: Hepatitis B
source: NVHCP: track HBsAg-positive mothers for institutional delivery and newborn HBIG; not a named PMSMA category – doctor may choose moderate

label: Previous surgery on the uterus (e.g. myomectomy)
source: MoHFW SBA/ANC guidelines: previous surgery on the reproductive tract; WHO FANC classifying form

label: Other liver disease / jaundice
source: MoHFW SBA systemic illness list: jaundice

label: Anaemia (severity not recorded)
source: PMSMA: only severe anaemia (Hb < 7 g/dL) is high risk – the measured Hb of this pregnancy is checked by its own rules below

label: Asthma
source: ACOG / NICE: severe or poorly controlled asthma is higher risk; GoI treats systemic illness as high – doctor to confirm level

label: Gestational diabetes (GDM) in this pregnancy
source: MoHFW PMSMA HRP list: gestational diabetes mellitus; FOGSI-GESTOSIS-ICOG HDP GCPR 2019 – doctor to confirm

label: High blood pressure in this pregnancy (gestational hypertension / pre-eclampsia)
source: MoHFW PMSMA HRP list: pregnancy-induced hypertension; Extended PMSMA Guidance Note section F; FOGSI-GESTOSIS-ICOG HDP GCPR 2019 – doctor to confirm

label: Twins or more
source: MoHFW PMSMA HRP list: twins / multiple pregnancy; MoHFW SBA/ANC guidelines; FOGSI-GESTOSIS-ICOG HDP GCPR 2019 – doctor to confirm

label: Low-lying placenta / placenta praevia
source: PMSMA criteria as used in PMSMA-based studies: low-lying placenta or placenta praevia. A placenta that is low before 32 weeks often moves up: untick it after a normal follow-up scan – doctor to confirm

label: Bleeding in this pregnancy
source: MoHFW SBA/ANC guidelines: antepartum haemorrhage; WHO antenatal classifying form: vaginal bleeding. Light early bleeding that has settled may be lower risk – doctor to confirm level

label: Severe anaemia: lowest Hb in this pregnancy under 7 g/dL
source: MoHFW PMSMA HRP list: severe anaemia (Hb < 7 g/dL); Anemia Mukt Bharat (2018). Uses the lowest Hb of this pregnancy, so it stays after treatment – doctor to confirm (the doctor can override the level)

label: Anaemia: lowest Hb in this pregnancy under 11 g/dL
source: MoHFW / Anemia Mukt Bharat: anaemia in pregnancy is Hb < 11 g/dL (mild 10–10.9, moderate 7–9.9); WHO 2024: < 11 in the first and third trimesters, < 10.5 in the second; Extended PMSMA tracks anaemia. Mild anaemia is very common: the doctor may lower the cut-off to 10 – doctor to confirm

label: Latest blood pressure: upper number 140 or more
source: MoHFW PMSMA HRP list: pregnancy-induced hypertension (BP 140/90 or higher); MoHFW SBA guidelines ask for two readings. This uses one reading (the latest): recheck, and when confirmed tick “High blood pressure in this pregnancy” – doctor to confirm level

label: Latest blood pressure: lower number 90 or more
source: MoHFW PMSMA HRP list: pregnancy-induced hypertension (BP 140/90 or higher); MoHFW SBA guidelines: diastolic 90 or more. This uses one reading (the latest): recheck, and when confirmed tick “High blood pressure in this pregnancy” – doctor to confirm level
